debate.text: Kestleford's hospice has 12 beds and night nurses who visit dying people at home. The board will pay £1.9 million and it costs £2.32 million. Closing beds, ending night visits or asking families for gifts each crossed a red line. I sent it back. I will not ask a dying person to lose out to a gap of £420,000. The board has to put its numbers in front of the town.

Tunde, ending night visits means sacking or moving night nurses, and those are people on shifts nobody else wants. I know what a shift change does to a family. Do not make the nurses the answer to the board's sum. Pay them for the hours and keep the visits.

I looked at the £150,000 for rent, heating and office. The gift plan wanted £120,000 cut from it. That is four fifths of the bill for keeping 12 beds warm. A hospice that is cold in January is not a hospice. Trim lights, not heat, and say what it saves per year.

Night visits matter for another reason. A person dying at home needs a home that is warm and safe. If the hospice cuts the visits, those cases land on housing and on the district nurse. It is not saved, it is moved. The board should count that before it calls the sum final.
Bea has it. A cut that only moves the cost is not a cut. Back to the board, with the gap, the guessed costs marked as guesses, and a date.
